jobs.description:
About SpotOn

We’re not just building restaurant tech, we’re giving independent restaurants the tools to compete and win. From our award-winning point-of-sale to AI-powered profit tools, everything we do helps operators boost profit, work smarter, and keep their best people. And every solution is backed by real humans who actually give a sh*t about helping restaurants succeed.

Named the #1 Restaurant POS by G2 (Summer 2026), based on ratings from real users
Rated the top-rated point-of-sale (POS) for restaurants, bars, retail, and small businesses by Capterra users
Awarded Great Places to Work and Built In’s Best Workplaces for multiple years running

We move fast, care hard, and fight for independent restaurant operators to do what they love, and love doing it. If you’re looking to make an impact with heart and hustle, SpotOn is the place for you.

Senior Data Analyst,

This is a hybrid position, 3-4x
/week in our San Francisco office.

Why this role exists

Behind every renewal, cancellation, software adoption, and support conversation is an opportunity to better understand what helps our merchants succeed. This role exists to turn those signals into action.

You'll help SpotOn understand the moments that matter throughout a merchant's journey, from their first interaction with our platform to go-live, and long-term success. You'll uncover what helps merchants thrive, where we can improve, and how we can build better experiences at every stage. Your work will influence decisions across Customer Experience, Sales, Finance, Product, and Engineering.

The impact you'll have

Retention is one of the highest-leverage opportunities at SpotOn. Every improvement means more merchants growing their business with us, stronger recurring revenue, and better products built from real customer insights.

As the owner of merchant retention and SaaS analytics, you'll help shape how we measure success, prioritize investments, and make decisions across the company. It's an opportunity to influence strategy through data.

Our team

You'll join a Finance & Data Analytics team where ownership is part of how we work. We build systems that make trusted insights available to everyone, helping teams spend less time finding answers and more time helping merchants succeed.

What You’ll Accomplish

You'll own the analytics that power SpotOn's merchant retention and SaaS business.

You'll

Identify the drivers behind merchant retention, churn, and software adoption.
Build trusted metrics, dashboards, and analyses used by executives and cross-functional leaders.
Partner with Product, Customer Success, Finance, Sales, and Engineering to turn insights into action.
Create scalable reporting, data models, and AI-powered workflows that reduce manual work and improve decision making.
Measure the impact of retention initiatives so we invest in what works.

Some weeks you'll spend hours in SQL untangling a complex problem. Other weeks you'll present recommendations to executives, automate recurring analyses, or build tools that eliminate repetitive work.

Success in this role is measured by the decisions you help the business make, and ultimately, by merchants who stay, grow, and succeed with SpotOn. If you see a problem worth solving, you have the ownership to solve it and the support to make it happen.

You should apply if you…

Notice when a merchant, a process, or a metric doesn't add up and treat that as an opportunity.
Aren't satisfied stopping at "churn is up" - you need to know why, down to the root cause, even when the answer is uncomfortable.
Like going deep enough to become the person people ask about a problem, but know when "good enough" beats another week of polish.
Aren't afraid to pick up a new tool, language, or AI assistant mid-project if it gets you to the answer faster.
Enjoy tinkering with AI coding tools like Claude Code/Codex as a way to move faster on real analysis.
Want your work to outlive the request it came from - you'd rather build the dashboard or create a scalable process after answering the same questions too many times
Believe in data-driven decisions, but have the judgment to know when the data isn't there yet and a decision still has to be made.
Have a track record of working well across Finance, Sales and Customer Success because the best answer to a retention question rarely lives in one team.

What We're Looking For

5+ years of experience in Analytics, Business Intelligence, or a related analytical role, ideally with experience in the Software industry.
Advanced SQL skills with experience working in cloud data warehouses (Snowflake preferred).
Experience with customer retention analyses
Experience building dashboards and reporting in Power BI or similar BI tools.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to investigate complex business questions.
Experience translating data into clear business recommendations.
Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
Experience with Python, dbt, AI coding assistants, or workflow automation tools is a plus.
Excellent communication skills and a collaborative mindset.
Bonus Point: Experience with Netsuite (or comparable ERP), SaaS metrics, subscription businesses

Compensation

Our base pay range is $150,000-$170,000 for this role
Please note the salary range listed is just one component of a competitive compensation package, which includes a company stock plan
Offers will be reflective of the candidate’s location and experience.

Benefits

At SpotOn, we put people above everything else. We’re known for our innovative software and technology solutions, but we stand out because of the hard-working humans behind the tech. We can’t take care of our clients without taking care of our employees first, and that’s why we invest in you with a competitive benefits package which includes:

Mainspring Energy manufactures and delivers fuel-flexible, low-emissions local power solutions that rapidly add new capacity and deliver reliable, affordable, and sustainable electric power. Pragmatic Optimism

Excellence without Ego

You are detail-oriented, proactive, and thrive in a fast-paced environment where you can combine technical rigor with practical execution.

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related technical field

POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Sustainability Program Coordinator is a position on GPCOG’s Sustainability Team that will bring expertise in floodplain management, municipal climate action, and project management to support successful delivery of a portfolio of emission reduction and climate resilience projects. The role will be a balance of supporting development of new programs and delivering technical expertise on existing programs. This position will report to the Sustainability Program Manager and will interact with diverse stakeholders, including internal GPCOG staff teams, municipal staff from GPCOG’s member communities, regional non-profits and businesses, funders, vendors, State agencies, and elected and appointed officials.
The Sustainability Team at GPCOG is a leader in climate change mitigation and resilience in Maine. Joining this small team provides an opportunity to create change at a community level and lead regional action that reduces emissions, builds resilience to climate impacts, and prepares the region for the climate crisis. This is a dynamic and fast-paced team that is looking for someone who thrives working on a variety of projects across all aspects of climate action.

Assist communities with interpreting and complying with National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) floodplain regulations.
Lead education and outreach to communities about floodplain mapping and mitigation strategies.
Obtain and maintain floodplain management certification (training provided).

Collect and analyze data to draw conclusions that support our program activities. This includes climate data and greenhouse gas emissions, sea level rise information, social and economic indicators, and land use data.
Organize and present data in the best manner possible to convey information, through maps, charts, graphs, etc. 
Write technical recommendations and reports and design impactful presentations.
Execute community engagement events, surveys, and presentations to bring data to the public, elected officials, and municipal staff and solicit feedback and input.
Manage reporting and financial flows and evaluate and report on project results.

Create educational and informational materials on sustainability programs including floodplain management, emergency preparedness, electrification, and climate resilience.
Draft and coordinate public engagement materials, including social media posts, press releases, and newsletters to support programs.  

4. Attend public meetings, public events and municipal meetings, in person, occasionally off hours or on weekends.
5. Support the task assignment, mentorship, and professional growth of emerging professionals and recent college graduates participating in GPCOG’s Resilience Corps Fellowship program. 

What you bring

At least 4-6 years’ experience in a professional setting, demonstrating possession of the required knowledge, skills, and abilities. 
Knowledge of and demonstrated experience with effective climate action strategies that reduce greenhouse gases and build resilience to climate change.
Strong writing, copy editing, and presenting skills.

Experience with GIS.

About Healthy Lifestars:
Healthy LifeStars® (HLS) is a national nonprofit organization whose mission is to motivate and educate kids to live active, healthy lives now and in the future. Working in partnership with schools and youth-serving organizations, Healthy LifeStars® delivers The LifeStar® Challenge a proven program that combines physical activity, nutrition education, and goal setting to empower elementary-aged children to build lasting healthy habits.

We believe that lasting change starts in communities with coaches who care, schools that show up, and children who feel empowered to make healthy choices every day. That belief is at the heart of everything we do and everything we look for in the people who join our team.

Position Overview
: Healthy LifeStars® is seeking a passionate and community-rooted  Western Region Program Coordinator
 to support and strengthen program delivery across Arizona and Colorado. This is a hybrid position, a blend of working from home and working directly in the community, for 35 hours per week.

The ideal candidate is based in the  Phoenix, AZ
 or  Denver, CO
 metro area and brings firsthand knowledge of the communities, schools, and youth-serving organizations we are working to reach. You do not just understand our mission from the outside , you have lived it, worked in it, or built something within it. That connection is not a bonus; it is central to what we are looking for.

Compensation ranges from $3,400 to $3,800 per month depending on experience. This position begins as a full-time contractor role with the opportunity to transition to a full-time permanent position. Reports to the National Program Director.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Program Coordination & Support

•      Support the onboarding and coordination of schools, afterschool programs, and youth-serving organizations implementing The LifeStar® Challenge
•      Conduct outreach to prospective program partners and share information about The LifeStar® Challenge and its benefits
•      Assist with securing site agreements and ensuring successful program launch and implementation at new partner sites
•      Provide ongoing implementation support and light coaching to program sites throughout the school year
•      Conduct regular site visits to build relationships, support program fidelity, and gather stories and data
•      Track and report program metrics in coordination with the national office using Notion (our program management platform)
•      Share insights and feedback to inform continuous program improvement

Community Engagement & Representation

•      Represent Healthy LifeStars® at local education events, health fairs, conferences, and community gatherings
•      Build and maintain genuine relationships with school leaders, educators, nonprofit partners, and community stakeholders
•      Serve as a local ambassador for Healthy LifeStars®, someone who is known, trusted, and connected in the communities we serve
•      Attend school and community events as a visible HLS presence (open houses, parent nights, assemblies, health fairs, etc.)
•      Participate in bi-monthly networking sessions to grow the HLS partner pipeline in your region

Coach & Partner Support

•      Maintain monthly touchpoints with every active coach in your region.
•      Support coaches in completing the monthly program survey and follow up directly with those who miss it
•      Identify and cultivate strong coach relationships that can serve as the foundation for success stories and student spotlights
•      Work with coaches and school leaders to select one student per core state to follow as a Student Spotlight throughout the program — documenting their journey in three chapters (beginning, mid-year, and end of year)
•      Collect at least one coach success story per semester and submit to the National Program Director and Communications team for use in newsletters, social media, and grant reporting

Organizational Support

•      Assist with community-based events celebrating student participation and program milestones (periodic and seasonal)
•      Provide limited support for fundraising or cultivation events as requested (e.g., Step Up for Kids™ or local engagement activities)
•      Submit monthly regional progress report by the first Monday of each month
•      Keep Notion updated weekly with all outreach, partner status, site visit logs, and coach survey tracking
•      Support additional program-related duties as outlined by the National Program Director

Qualifications:

Required

•      Enthusiastic self-starter with a genuine passion for youth health, wellness, and the Healthy LifeStars® mission
•      2–3 years of relevant experience in education, youth services, nonprofit programming, or community engagement
•      Prior experience working in or alongside the communities HLS serves — including schools, youth programs, or health-focused organizations in the Phoenix or Denver metro area
•      Strong organizational skills and ability to manage tasks, timelines, and relationships independently
•      Comfortable communicating with educators, school leaders, and community partners at all levels
•      Strong verbal and written communication skills
•      Reliable transportation and willingness to travel locally for site visits and events
•      Ability to work remotely with reliable internet and phone access
•      Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of experience, education, and training

Strongly Preferred

•      Background in K–12 education, physical education, school administration, or school-based programming
•      Experience building community partnerships, running outreach campaigns, or growing a partner network from the ground up
•      Existing relationships with schools, nonprofits, or youth-serving organizations in the Phoenix or Denver area
•      Familiarity with Notion, Google Workspace, or similar project management and collaboration tools
